deepdive.sec: Power / Grid Equipment & Energy Transition (the **OEM / demand side**)

bull_bear.body:
- Industrial Systems margin (railways pricing, commodity); semiconductor cash drain until it scales.
- Receivables rising with power growth (90–100 day terms).
- Commodity inflation (motors/PVC); tariff impact in some export geographies (consciously slowed some).
- Execution/quality is the stated differentiator as capacity scales fast.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, execution-focused ("Amrit Kaal"); aggressive but disciplined capacity build; candid on industrial margin drag and semiconductor investment. Strong ROCE (22% / power 100%+).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **CG is the demand keystone for the whole folder:** a transformer OEM scaling capacity 17k→110k MVA is exactly what drives the bushing (Yash), CTC/winding-wire (KSH/Apar/Bhagyanagar) and transformer-oil (Apar) shortages. Its +91% power backlog is the cleanest single proxy for the cycle's durability.
- CG is *also* a **RIP-bushing localizer** (named by Yash) — partial vertical integration into the scarce component.
- Power-side **ROCE >100%** + 22–24% margins = the most profitable expression of the cycle in the set; semiconductor is the wildcard.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Market leader in the electrical engineering industry with a diversified product range across business lines
- Extensive channel-partner network delivering strong market penetration/outreach
- Cutting-edge, automated manufacturing facilities (manufacturing excellence)
- Ongoing capacity expansion to capture economies of scale
- Lean cost structure combined with proven capability to deliver customised solutions
- Part of the Murugappa Group (since November 2020) with 89-year operating legacy and 22 manufacturing facilities across India and Europe
- CG EDGE operating model embedding operational excellence, commercial rigour, digital enablement and execution discipline, cited by management as a competitive asset not reflected on the balance sheet
- Strong, growing order book (standalone backlog of Rs.15,719 Cr, up 59% YoY) providing multi-quarter revenue visibility
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Legacy investigations by CBI, SFIO and Enforcement Directorate into past-period affairs of the Company and its Subsidiaries, relating to erstwhile Promoters/Directors, remain in progress. — An unresolved regulatory/legal overhang from the pre-Murugappa management continues into FY26; the Company states it is extending full co-operation, but outcome and any potential liability remain undisclosed and open.
- Enterprise risk exposure explicitly spans financial, operational, sectoral, technological, ESG-specific, cybersecurity and geopolitical domains. — The Company itself frames this breadth as material enough to warrant a Board-approved Risk Management Charter & Policy and a dedicated Risk Management Committee, reflecting multi-domain risk concentration across a diversified, geographically spread global business.
- The semiconductor vertical (CG Semi and the Axiro Semiconductor Group) remains loss-making while capacity is still under construction/ramp. — CG Semi recorded a loss before tax of Rs.80.28 crores in FY26 while its Main Plant (G2) OSAT facility is still under construction (expected by end-CY2026), and the Axiro Semiconductor Group recorded a loss before tax of Rs.30.83 crores after acquiring the Fabless Semiconductor design business from Renesas Electronics America Inc. for Rs.284.13 crores during the year; a capital-intensive, pre-profitability vertical is a drag on near-term consolidated returns and carries execution/integration risk.
- Return ratios (RONW and ROCE) declined year-on-year because QIP proceeds sit in the capital base ahead of full deployment. — Company explicitly attributes the RONW decline (23.96% to 16.03%) and ROCE decline (33.34% to 22.08%) to undeployed QIP capital being included in net worth/capital employed — a transitional capital-efficiency drag until the funded transformer, switchgear and OSAT projects are commissioned and generate returns.
- Working-capital efficiency weakened, with turnover ratios declining and debtor/inventory days lengthening. — Average debtor days rose from 65 to 74 and inventory days from 48 to 54 in FY26, while net sales to gross/net working capital turns fell (partly QIP-fund related per the Company's own remarks) — a point to monitor as the business scales into large capex-funded capacity.

business.body:

business.body: CG (headquartered in Mumbai) offers a diversified portfolio of transformers, switchgears, motors, drives, railway systems, consumer electrical products (fans etc.), and RF semiconductor solutions, serving industrial, infrastructure, utility, transportation, and consumer applications across domestic and international markets. The business is organised into two segments: Industrial Systems (Motors, Drives and Automation, Railways, and Fast Moving Electrical Goods) and Power Systems (Transformers, Switchgears and Other Allied Products), supplemented by an emerging semiconductor solutions vertical (Axiro, CG Semi).

outlook.body:
- **Power demand "huge all over the world"; domestic ex-large-orders growing ~15–20%** ("the game has just started"). Utilities/govt "give us more, give us more."
- **Transformer capacity:** Gwalior 6k→10k MVA; Bhopal/Mandideep →40k→**65k MVA** (lean); **Greenfield commissioning Jul–Aug 2026** (25–30k → 45k MVA by CY-end) → **~110,000 MVA total by end-CY26**, across all ratings to **765kV (new plant up to 1,200kV)**.
- **GIS:** 400kV commercialization in **FY27** (type-test Q2–Q3); 765kV "in conversation." GIS market ~₹12,000cr (24–30% GIS, rest AIS).
- **Motors:** double-digit (50/50 price/volume); IE3/IE4 adoption slow in India but expected to pick up. Drives: new AMX launches; LV drives ~100% indigenous.
- **Exports & services:** key focus; order bookings >doubled YoY.
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body:
- Standalone backlog **₹15,719cr (+59%)**, consol ₹17,107cr (+61%) → strong FY27 revenue visibility.
- **₹900cr hyperscaler data-centre transformer order** (12–20 month delivery, FAS Mumbai). Power-side credit ~90–100 days (drives receivables).
- G.G. Tronics (railway signalling): backlog ~₹1,000cr; passenger trials nearly done → execution starts ~1–1.5 months.

outlook.body:
- **Data centres:** hyperscaler transformer order (₹900cr) + pursuing US grid utilities.
- **GIS** (400→765kV), **HVDC-class transformers** (new plant to 1,200kV).

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Purpose 'Pioneering Innovation for a Sustainable Future' and the CG EDGE operating model (operational excellence, commercial rigour, digital enablement, innovation, high-performance culture) are positioned as the durable execution engine behind margin expansion and delivery discipline, described as 'not a programme with an end date'.
- Pursuing global scale deliberately: manufacturing capacity (transformers, semiconductors) is being sized for global, not just Indian, demand; export order bookings more than doubled YoY and CG is leaning into India's expanding FTA network to grow addressable export markets.
- Long-horizon entry into semiconductors via Axiro (design) and CG Semi (OSAT manufacturing), explicitly framed as a 'long-gestation business that demands patient capital, technological depth and sustained execution' rather than a near-term earnings driver.
- Railways margin recovery plan on three fronts: operational efficiency improvements, building a dedicated services vertical intended to structurally lift margins over time, and an active new product development agenda.
- Continued capacity expansion in Power Systems (transformers, switchgear) to capture what management characterises as structural, multi-year demand for power infrastructure, both domestic and export.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Power Systems: Board-approved Greenfield Transformer manufacturing facility of 45,000 MVA capacity in Western India (Sehore District, Madhya Pradesh; ~45.13 acres allotted by MPIDC on a 99-year lease), estimated cost Rs.712 crores (net of taxes), work currently in progress; the facility is expected to commission in Q2FY27, initially adding 25,000-30,000 MVA and ramping to 45,000 MVA over subsequent quarters, taking total transformer capacity to approximately 1,20,000 MVA (up from ~23,000 MVA a year earlier, already expanded to almost 75,000 MVA during FY26). A separate Greenfield Switchgear manufacturing facility was approved in Western India to double existing switchgear capacity (MV/EHV switchgear, Substation Automation Systems, Power Electronics), estimated cost Rs.748.20 crores (net of taxes), on ~35 acres with ~72,000 sq. m built-up area, expected to complete within 33 months of land identification/allotment, funded through internal accruals, equity and/or debt. Semiconductors: CG Semi inaugurated India's first end-to-end OSAT facility (G1) at Sanand, Gujarat in August 2025, now operational at a peak capacity of 0.5 million units per day, with plans to scale to 14.5 million chips per day via an upcoming G2 facility; the combined G1+G2 project represents an estimated investment of approximately Rs.7,600 crores and is expected to generate approximately 5,000 direct and indirect jobs, enabled by fiscal support from the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) and the Gujarat State Electronics Mission (GSEM). Axiro (semiconductor design subsidiary) generated approximately Rs.500 crores of revenue in FY26, anchored by the RF business acquired from Renesas Electronics, and CG has invested in EdgeCortix to build AI-driven semiconductor design capabilities via targeted partnerships. The Rs.3,000 crore QIP raised in July 2025 is being deployed into the greenfield transformer and switchgear facilities and the OSAT facility. Separately, the Company entered a joint-development agreement with Skyboard Realty Private Limited (a K Raheja Corp group company) for redevelopment of its 'CG House' property in Worli, Mumbai; demolition of the building started during the year, and the registered office relocated to One Unity Center, Prabhadevi, Mumbai with effect from 9 December 2025.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global power sector transformation - accelerating energy transition, grid modernisation, and rising electricity demand from data centres, industrial expansion and electrification - translating into sustained, multi-year demand for transformers, switchgear and grid solutions.
- Structural, multi-decade themes cited as durable rather than cyclical: India's energy transition, railway modernisation, the rise of data centres and electronics manufacturing, and India's growing role in global manufacturing.
- Global structural forces: proliferation of AI infrastructure, the drive toward higher industrial energy efficiency, and reconfiguration of semiconductor supply chains.
- Industrial Systems demand supported by modernisation and infrastructure creation, expansion of manufacturing in electronics, chemicals and renewable energy, and rising adoption of automation and energy-efficient systems.
- Motors market transitioning from volume-led to value-led demand, with customers prioritising performance, lifecycle efficiency and application-specific solutions; incremental demand emerging from data centres (HVAC, cooling, high-efficiency motors), electric mobility and renewable installations.
- Indian Railways' network expansion, modernisation and safety initiatives creating structural, long-duration demand for traction systems, propulsion technology and railway safety solutions.
- Macro tailwinds: India GDP grew an estimated 7.3% in FY26 (IMF), projected to moderate to 6.5% in FY27; India's expanding FTA network (UK, EFTA, Oman, New Zealand concluded in FY26) widening export market access for Indian-manufactured industrial and power products.
- Headwinds flagged: commodity volatility (copper, steel, crude oil) and tightened supply chains from the Middle East conflict; intensifying competition across CG's segments; Railways margins remain 'a work in progress' reflecting competitive pricing dynamics and mix.
- Standalone order intake of Rs.17,574 Cr, up 30% YoY, with a closing order backlog of Rs.15,719 Cr, up 59% YoY, described as providing strong multi-quarter revenue visibility into FY27 and beyond.
- Consolidated order intake of Rs.19,616 Cr, with a closing unexecuted order book of Rs.17,107 Cr, offering 'a solid foundation for future growth'.
- Export order bookings more than doubled year-on-year; the single largest order in CG's history was a Rs.900 Cr contract to supply power transformers for a hyperscale data centre in the United States.
- Power Systems won the largest single domestic transformer order in CG's history, from PowerGrid Corporation, alongside its largest single export transformer order (from a US data centre customer).
- G.G. Tronics, CG's railway safety systems subsidiary, entered FY26 with a healthy order backlog.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: The diversified transformer + switchgear **OEM** at the centre of the grid super-cycle — *"Amrit Kaal for the power sector."* Record FY26 (standalone +21% rev, PBT +39%); **Power Systems exploding** (FY rev +46%, order backlog **+91% YoY**, 22–24% PBIT margins). **Transformer capacity ramping 17k → 110k MVA** in ~2 yrs, up to 765kV (new plant to 1,200kV). It's the **demand engine** that pulls bushings, CTC/winding wire, transformer oil and switchgear components — i.e. the buyer behind the other names' shortages. Semiconductor build-out is the long-dated optionality (and a near-term drag).

meta.thesis: The diversified transformer + switchgear **OEM** at the centre of the grid super-cycle — *"Amrit Kaal for the power sector."* Record FY26 (standalone +21% rev, PBT +39%); **Power Systems exploding** (FY rev +46%, order backlog **+91% YoY**, 22–24% PBIT margins). **Transformer capacity ramping 17k → 110k MVA** in ~2 yrs, up to 765kV (new plant to 1,200kV). It's the **demand engine** that pulls bushings, CTC/winding wire, transformer oil and switchgear components — i.e. the buyer behind the other names' shortages. Semiconductor build-out is the long-dated optionality (and a near-term drag).
